primary_claim: Proposes 'Semantic Temperature', a method that projects candidate output tokens into a latent semantic space (via PC1 reduction using a smaller interpreter LLM), reorders them by semantic polarity, and applies temperature to a normal distribution over that ordering rather than to raw token probabilities, so that low-temperature sampling concentrates on the model's 'median semantic intent' instead of the single highest-probability token, aiming to reduce hallucinations caused by vote-splitting across synonymous high-probability tokens.
stated_future_work: Determine how to give temperature as an input to the neural network itself, rather than applying it at the interpreter level

Develop a safe separation of inputs and outputs from the LLM so it produces no output until it reaches an acceptable confidence level, while still allowing review of its thought process for alignment validation
limitations_stated: This approach is only a band-aid applied to currently-deployed LLMs; temperature should ideally be applied at the model level rather than the interpreter level

Look-ahead semantic sampling improves the interpreter's capability but requires the larger model to produce many outputs per token selected, so only 1-2 tokens of look-ahead is recommended to balance effectiveness against computational cost
quote: Semantic Temperature application works to resolve this by rewriting the temperature script to identify the “median” semantic intent behind what the model was communicating
